name: Learn drink mixing with nonalcoholic ingredients
blurb: The craft of a good drink is balance, dilution and texture — none of which require alcohol. Learn the ratios and you can build anything.
gear: Citrus juicer and a good knife
Sugar for syrups, plus bitters-style aromatics, teas and sodas
steps: Learn the sour template: two parts base, one part citrus, three-quarters part sweet — and taste how shifting each changes the result.
Make a simple syrup, then flavoured ones with herbs or spices. Syrups are where nonalcoholic drinks get their body.
Learn to shake properly: hard, with plenty of ice, for 12 to 15 seconds — this chills, dilutes and aerates.
Learn when to stir instead: any drink without citrus or dairy, for a silkier texture.
Learn to replace the weight alcohol provides using strong tea, verjuice, saline solution or a splash of vinegar-based shrub.
Build a repertoire of five drinks and learn to garnish with expressed citrus oils.
tips: Fresh citrus only. Bottled juice is the fastest way to a mediocre drink.
Dilution is an ingredient, not a mistake. Under-shaken drinks taste harsh and thin.
Salt or acid is usually what a flat nonalcoholic drink is missing.
proof: You build five balanced drinks by ratio, without a recipe, and adjust one on the fly by taste.
